## Featured Project

### Forecasting and Explaining U.S. Unemployment Through Macroeconomic Indicators

Built a reproducible forecasting and historical-correlation workflow using six public U.S. macroeconomic series covering **April 1956 through December 2025**. The analysis compares six algorithms at 3-, 6-, and 12-month horizons using chronological validation, persistence and unemployment-only baselines, and separate lead–lag correlation analysis.

The selected **3-month Ridge Regression** model achieved **MAE 0.349, RMSE 1.020, and R² 0.720**. The selected **6-month Extra Trees** model achieved **R² 0.563**, while the 12-month model showed limited incremental value (**R² 0.205**). Consumer sentiment had the strongest overall external historical relationship with future unemployment.
